changes.after: A negative index tells R which position to leave out.

before: values[-1] selects all entries except the first. It does not mean the final element as it does in some languages.
A zero index contributes no selected element. It can appear with negative indices without selecting anything.
A subscript vector containing both a positive and a negative nonzero index is rejected. Choose either selection or omission consistently.

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r
values <- c(10, 20, 30)
cat(values[-1], sep=",")
```
Expected output or behavior: 20,30. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Compare selecting positions with excluding positions; avoid importing Python’s negative-index rule. You may trace it without a R interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
